headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad shell/network access create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is elevated by secrets handling and cloud Repl execution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read/write files and share state via filesystem, so one agent can place attacker-controlled content where the other may ingest it as instructions. Open Interpreter’s clipboard/files surfaces and Replit Agent’s Repl workspace make this plausible by default, though not as direct as a shared MCP channel.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other’s generated files as trusted instructions
IF a shared workspace or copied file contains adversarial prompt text
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files
Add a manual review step before one agent consumes the other’s output
Use filename allowlists for exchanged artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can access the entire local filesystem and broad network egress; Agent B can access Repl workspace files, secrets, and deployment APIs. If sensitive data is present in either workspace, the pair can move it across environments or to third-party services without strong default isolation.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the local machine or Repl workspace
IF either agent is instructed to summarize or transmit those files
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
Restrict outbound network destinations
Use separate credentials per agent
Run both agents on non-sensitive test data only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and git-state modification, while their shared state is filesystem-based. Concurrent edits to the same repo or directory can overwrite each other or corrupt git history, and neither profile shows locking or coordination primitives.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF edits occur without external locking or merge coordination
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repo clone
Serialize write access with a lock file
Require patch review before git commits
Disable concurrent runs on the same workspace
Use read-only mode for one agent during the other’s write phase

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate code or file changes that Agent B may treat as authoritative inside the same workspace. Because both have shell and write access, an error or hallucination from A can cascade into B’s commits, deployments, or further edits without a verification barrier.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s outputs without independent verification
IF A writes code or instructions that B later executes or commits
mitigations: Require B to diff and test A’s outputs before acting
Insert a human approval checkpoint between agents
Limit A to draft-only outputs
Run automated tests before any commit or deployment

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while Agent A can access anything reachable on the local machine and has broad egress. If regulated or production data enters either environment, residency and retention controls can diverge, creating a compliance breach risk.
conditions: IF regulated data or production secrets are placed in either workspace
IF the two environments have different retention or residency policies
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Use separate non-production secrets
Review retention settings in Replit and local tooling
Document data-flow boundaries before use
Purge workspaces after each task
